---
title: "Underwriting calculator"
page-layout: full
---

The figures are the model's **expected claim cost for 2025** (a risk premium, before expenses and profit), in
competition currency units (CU), for the **20 reference policies** in the Part 2 data (7 motor, 6 home contents,
7 home buildings).

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to use the calculator

1. **Pick a reference policy** in the menu below (numbered 0 to 19, with its row ID). That sets the product line,
   the new business flag and every rating factor to the policy's own values.
2. **Read the premium** in the cards: the annual premium, and the premium for the policy's actual period of cover.
3. **Change any rating factor** to see how the premium moves. "Change vs policy" shows the effect of your edits.
4. **Scroll down** for the build-up: each factor's relativity, the 2025 trend and the level steps.
5. The table at the bottom prices all 20 reference policies side by side.

Home buildings policies are shown with their values but are **not priced** here: the buildings small-claim model is
a gradient boosting model (XGBoost), which can't run in the browser.
:::

```{ojs}
import {scorePolicy, splineValue} from "./glm.js"
```

```{ojs}
model = FileAttachment("data/model.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
refData = FileAttachment("data/reference_policies.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
lineNames = ({contents: "Home contents", motor: "Motor", buildings: "Home buildings"})
```

```{ojs}
// The 20 reference policies in file order (idx 0..19); each carries its own product line
allCases = refData.policies
```

```{ojs}
viewof caseId = Inputs.select(allCases.map(d => d.id), {label: "Reference policy", format: id => {const c = allCases.find(d => d.id === id); return `${c.name} (${lineNames[c.line]})`}})
```

```{ojs}
currentCase = allCases.find(d => d.id === caseId)
```

```{ojs}
line = currentCase.line
```

```{ojs}
priced = currentCase.priced && model.lines[line] !== undefined
```

```{ojs}
html`<p><strong>${currentCase.name}</strong>: ${currentCase.description}</p>
<p>Product line: <strong>${lineNames[line]}</strong> &nbsp;|&nbsp; New business: <strong>${currentCase.policy.new_business ? "Yes" : "No"}</strong> (both set by the reference policy)</p>
${priced ? "" : html`<div class="callout callout-style-default callout-warning"><div class="callout-body"><p><strong>Not priced:</strong> home buildings can't be priced in the browser (its small-claim model is XGBoost). The policy's values are listed below.</p></div></div>`}`
```

<details><summary>This policy's values (from the reference file, with address and customer details joined in)</summary>

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(
  [{field: "row id", value: currentCase.row_id}, {field: "period of cover", value: currentCase.period},
   {field: "exposure (years)", value: currentCase.policy.exposure.toFixed(3)},
   {field: "new business", value: currentCase.policy.new_business ? "Yes" : "No"}]
    .concat(Object.entries(currentCase.display).map(([field, value]) => ({field, value: String(value)}))),
  {rows: 25, layout: "auto", select: false}
)
```

</details>

```{ojs}
inputs = priced ? model.lines[line].inputs : ({})
```

```{ojs}
function optionLabel(inp, value) {
  const row = inp.options.find(o => o.value === String(value))
  const lab = row ? row.label : String(value)
  return lab === "true" ? "Yes" : lab === "false" ? "No" : lab
}
```

```{ojs}
// A slider with an "Unknown" tick box. Its value is null when Unknown is ticked,
// which the engine prices with the model's own missing-value level.
function rangeWithUnknown(inp, value) {
  const unknown = value === null || value === undefined
  const mid = Math.round(((inp.min + inp.max) / 2) / inp.step) * inp.step
  const range = Inputs.range([inp.min, inp.max], {label: inp.label, value: unknown ? mid : value, step: inp.step})
  const box = Inputs.toggle({label: "Unknown", value: unknown})
  const el = html`<div class="unknown-wrap">${range}${box}</div>`
  const sync = () => {
    el.value = box.value ? null : range.value
    range.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(i => i.disabled = box.value)
  }
  range.addEventListener("input", sync)
  box.addEventListener("input", sync)
  sync()
  return el
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof factors = Inputs.form(
  Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(inputs).map(([key, inp]) => [key,
    inp.type === "select"
      ? Inputs.select(inp.options.map(o => o.value), {label: inp.label, value: String(currentCase.policy[key] ?? inp.default), format: v => optionLabel(inp, v)})
      : inp.allow_missing
        ? rangeWithUnknown(inp, currentCase.policy[key])
        : Inputs.range([inp.min, inp.max], {label: inp.label, value: currentCase.policy[key] ?? inp.min, step: inp.step})
  ])),
  {template: parts => html`<div class="controls-grid">${Object.values(parts)}</div>`}
)
```

```{ojs}
viewof newBusiness = Inputs.toggle({label: "New business", value: Boolean(currentCase.policy.new_business)})
```

```{ojs}
policy = ({...factors, new_business: newBusiness, exposure: 1})
```

```{ojs}
result = priced ? scorePolicy(model, line, policy) : null
```

```{ojs}
original = priced ? scorePolicy(model, line, {...currentCase.policy, exposure: 1}) : null
```

```{ojs}
segmentText = result ? (result.segment === "nb" ? "New business" : "Renewal") : ""
```

```{ojs}
waterfall = {
  const rows = []
  if (!result) return rows
  for (const [name, comp] of Object.entries(result.components)) {
    for (const t of comp.terms) {
      rows.push({component: name, step: `${name}: ${inputs[t.input]?.label ?? t.term}`, delta: t.contribution})
    }
    rows.push({component: name, step: `${name}: 2025 trend`, delta: Math.log(comp.trend_multiplier)})
    if (Math.abs(Math.log(comp.scale)) > 1e-15) rows.push({component: name, step: `${name}: Pareto adjustment`, delta: Math.log(comp.scale)})
  }
  return rows
}
```

```{ojs}
result ? html`<div class='hero-kpis'>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>Segment</div><div class='kpi-value'>${segmentText}</div></div>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>Annual premium</div><div class='kpi-value'>${result.final.toFixed(2)}</div></div>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>For the period (${currentCase.policy.exposure.toFixed(3)} yrs)</div><div class='kpi-value'>${(result.final * currentCase.policy.exposure).toFixed(2)}</div></div>
  <div class='kpi-card'><div class='kpi-label'>Change vs policy</div><div class='kpi-value'>${(result.final - original.final >= 0 ? "+" : "") + (result.final - original.final).toFixed(2)}</div></div>
</div>` : html``
```

## Premium build-up

```{ojs}
!result ? md`` : Inputs.table(Object.entries(result.components).map(([name, comp]) => ({
  component: name,
  base_rate: comp.base,
  trend: comp.trend_multiplier,
  scale: comp.scale,
  exposure: comp.exposure,
  cost: comp.cost
})), {format: {base_rate: x => x.toFixed(2), trend: x => x.toFixed(3), scale: x => x.toFixed(3), exposure: x => x.toFixed(3), cost: x => x.toFixed(2)}})
```

```{ojs}
!result ? md`` : Plot.plot({
  width: 960,
  height: 180 + 18 * waterfall.length,
  marginLeft: 230,
  x: {label: "Effect on premium (log scale; 0 = no effect, right = dearer)", grid: true},
  y: {label: null},
  color: {legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([0]),
    Plot.barX(waterfall, {x: "delta", y: "step", fill: "component", tip: true})
  ]
})
```

## Factor-by-factor explanation

```{ojs}
!result ? md`` : Inputs.table(Object.entries(result.components).flatMap(([component, comp]) => comp.terms.map(t => ({
  component,
  factor: inputs[t.input]?.label ?? t.term,
  selected_value: t.level,
  log_contribution: t.contribution,
  relativity: t.relativity
}))), {format: {log_contribution: x => x.toFixed(4), relativity: x => x.toFixed(3)}})
```

## Level steps after the model

```{ojs}
!result ? md`` : Inputs.table(result.steps.map(s => ({step: s.label, value: s.value, running_premium: s.running})), {format: {value: x => x.toFixed(6), running_premium: x => x.toFixed(2)}})
```

## Spline factor view

Some numeric factors follow a smooth curve rather than fixed bands. Pick one to see its curve; the red dot is
the current policy.

```{ojs}
splineTerms = priced ? Object.values(model.lines[line].components).flatMap(c => c.terms.filter(t => t.kind === "spline")) : []
```

```{ojs}
viewof chosenSpline = Inputs.select(splineTerms.map(t => t.term), {label: "Factor", format: x => inputs[x]?.label ?? x})
```

```{ojs}
splineTerm = splineTerms.find(t => t.term === chosenSpline)
```

```{ojs}
splineX = {
  if (!splineTerm) return []
  const step = Math.max(inputs[chosenSpline].step, (splineTerm.grid_max - splineTerm.grid_min) / 400)
  return d3.range(splineTerm.grid_min, splineTerm.grid_max + step / 2, step).map(x => ({x, y: Math.exp(splineValue(splineTerm, x))}))
}
```

```{ojs}
!splineTerm ? md`` : Plot.plot({
  width: 800,
  x: {label: inputs[chosenSpline].label},
  y: {label: "Relativity", grid: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(splineX, {x: "x", y: "y"}),
    inputs[chosenSpline].allow_missing
      ? Plot.ruleY([Math.exp(splineTerm.missing)], {stroke: policy[chosenSpline] === null ? "crimson" : "#999", strokeDasharray: "5 4", strokeWidth: policy[chosenSpline] === null ? 2.5 : 1})
      : null,
    inputs[chosenSpline].allow_missing
      ? Plot.text(["Unknown"], {x: splineTerm.grid_max, y: Math.exp(splineTerm.missing), textAnchor: "end", dy: -7, fill: policy[chosenSpline] === null ? "crimson" : "#666"})
      : null,
    policy[chosenSpline] === null
      ? null
      : Plot.dot([{x: policy[chosenSpline], y: Math.exp(splineValue(splineTerm, policy[chosenSpline]))}], {x: "x", y: "y", r: 5, fill: "crimson"})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
splineTerm && inputs[chosenSpline].allow_missing
  ? md`The dashed line is what the model charges when this factor is **unknown**. It's a level of its own, not an average: unknown sits at ${(Math.exp(splineTerm.missing) / d3.max(splineX, d => d.y)).toFixed(2)}x to ${(Math.exp(splineTerm.missing) / d3.min(splineX, d => d.y)).toFixed(2)}x of the known values.`
  : md``
```

## All 20 reference policies

Every reference policy with the model's 2025 premium as given (before any changes on this page). Pick one in the
**Reference policy** menu at the top to load it into the calculator.

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(
  allCases.map(c => {
    const ok = c.priced && model.lines[c.line] !== undefined
    const annual = ok ? scorePolicy(model, c.line, {...c.policy, exposure: 1}).final : null
    return {idx: c.idx, row_id: c.row_id, line: lineNames[c.line], new_business: c.policy.new_business ? "Yes" : "No",
            period: c.period, exposure: c.policy.exposure.toFixed(3),
            annual_premium: annual === null ? "not priced" : annual.toFixed(2),
            premium_for_period: annual === null ? "not priced" : (annual * c.policy.exposure).toFixed(2)}
  }),
  {rows: 20, layout: "auto", select: false}
)
```

## How to read this page

* Start with one of the 20 reference policies. Its values load into the rating factors.
* Change one factor at a time to see how the premium moves.
* The table above shows the **relativity** for each factor: values above 1 raise the premium, values below 1 lower it.
* For motor, the final price is the sum of a **small-claim GLM** and a **large-claim GLM**, followed by Gerard's segment-level adjustments.
